_note: LOS SERVICIOS EXTERNOS — the ids and URLs that connect this game to something outside it: AdSense/AdMob, Play Billing, GA4 and the runtime content endpoint. Each one is a string that has to match a console entry somewhere else EXACTLY, and each one fails quietly when it does not.
_why_here: These are not secrets and they were never hidden — a publisher id and an ad unit id ship in the page source of every ad-supported site on the web, because the browser has to send them. Putting them in one versioned record is not about concealment; it is so that the four places a wrong id can bite are one place to check, and so the editor can show what the build is actually configured with rather than somebody grepping four modules.
_secrets: NOTHING SECRET GOES IN THIS FILE. It is bundled into the client, so anything here is public by construction. A signing keystore, a Play service-account key or a server token belongs outside the repo — see the Android section of CLAUDE.md.

ads._note: LOS ANUNCIOS, y son DOS SISTEMAS DISTINTOS que este juego trata como uno. La web usa H5 Games Ads (la API `adBreak` de AdSense) y la app usa AdMob: distintos ids, distintos nombres de espacio, distinta forma de pedir un anuncio. Antes estaban mezclados en un solo bloque plano, que es cómo un id de la app termina donde iba uno de la web.
ads._policy: LA MISMA SUPERFICIE AMABLE EN LOS DOS LADOS, y eso es una decisión de producto y no un default: la app es primero una vitrina turística. Intersticial sólo cada N corridas TERMINADAS, nunca en las primeras que alguien juega, nunca a media corrida, nunca después del tutorial. Rewarded 100 % pedido por el jugador. Y CERO banners: taparían la calle mientras uno maneja.

policy.graceNote: no interstitial at all for a player's first runs — somebody deciding whether they like this game should not meet an ad while deciding
policy.bannersNote: NOT a placeholder for 'not yet'. A banner covers the road while driving; that is the reason, and it does not change with revenue.

web._note: H5 Games Ads — the AdSense Ad Placement API. It serves once the site is approved in AdSense with H5 Games Ads enabled; until then every `adBreak` call is a silent no-op and the game simply continues, which is why nothing here needs a fallback.
web.frequencyHintNote: a pacing safety net ON TOP of `policy.interstitialEvery` — the two are independent and the stricter one wins
web._placementNote: `name` is what shows up in the AdSense reports, so renaming one loses the history behind it. `type` is the API's own vocabulary (`next`, `reward`, `start`, `pause`, `browse`) and only the two used here are implemented.
web.rewardTimeoutNote: belt and braces: `adBreakDone` is documented to always fire, including on no-fill, but a promise that never settles would hang the results screen

app._note: AdMob through @capacitor-community/admob, dynamically imported so it never enters the web bundle.
app.applicationIdNote: THIS IS NOT READ AT RUNTIME — it lives in android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml, which is where the SDK reads it. It is recorded here so the two cannot drift, and `tests/test_services.py` compares them. A mismatch means the app initialises against the wrong account and every ad silently no-fills.
app._unused: No banner, appOpen or native unit, deliberately — see `policy.banners`. A unit id added here with nothing asking for it is drift; the placement has to exist in `ads.js` too.
app.testDevicesNote: register a device in the AdMob console for ad-debugging rather than swapping ids in the source — swapping ids is how a test id ships

iap._note: Play Billing. `removeAds` is NON-consumable — it is owned forever once bought — while the coin packs in `economy.json` are consumable. Getting that backwards is the difference between selling something once and selling it every time.

analytics._note: GA4. Empty means OFF, and that is the shipped state: the module no-ops entirely without an id, so nothing is sent and no script is loaded until somebody pastes one in. `VITE_GA_ID` in `.env.local` overrides it for a local test.

content._note: The runtime content endpoint — sponsors, the theme, authored copy and now authored sounds. THE ONE THING IN THIS GAME THAT IS FETCHED RATHER THAN BUNDLED: everything else, including all 640 world tiles and every registry, is compiled into the bundle at build time.
content._integrity: Because it is fetched, it is the only surface where what the game runs is not what the build produced. `remote.js` validates every field it reads — colours are length-capped, strings are truncated, a sound's steps are clamped to a safe range — rather than trusting the payload.

links._note: Where the game sends a player who wants to support it.
